audit.whatIsWrong: Two problems. (a) The chart reads Skill, Kayle, Kayle, Skill, Skill, Kayle, Kayle in both layers; the packet reads Skill, K'Sante, Kayle, Kayle, Kayle, Kayle, K'Sante, and the prose backs the packet on rows 1, 4 and 6 — whys[1] has him walking you down, mid calls level 6 the flip, and whys[6]/spikes[3]/late all say 2+ items is his. (b) The whys array is shifted a row: whys[2], labelled Level 3, describes Divine Ascent and Divine Judgment, which are level-6 abilities; whys[4], labelled Level 6, describes the Nashor's timing; whys[5], labelled First item, describes holding R.
audit.why: The shift means the page prints the level-6 power spike under Level 3 — a player reads that their autos go ranged three levels before they do, walks up in melee range, and dies to Ntofo Strikes into Path Maker.
audit.corrected: Rows 1, 4 and 6 flipped as matched full/content pairs (K'Sante, Kayle, K'Sante). whys[2..5] re-seated so each row's reasoning describes its own level: L3 = his Q/W cadence, L4-5 = Path Maker's true damage, L6 = the ranged flip, first item = Nashor's plus anti-heal.
sources: existing whys[1], whys[6], mid, late, spikes[3]

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 spike is described under Level 3 and no cooldowns anchor any of it. All Out is 120/100/80 and Path Maker 14/13/12/11/10; neither number appears.
audit.why: 'Trade when All Out is down' is the page's central instruction and it is unusable without knowing the window is 80 seconds at rank 3, or that Path Maker's charge is the 14s tell at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Ntofo Strikes' 3.5s and 450 range, Path Maker's 14s, and All Out's 80s written into the re-seated whys.
sources: enemyKit Q cd 3.5 range 450, W cd 14/13/12/11/10, R cd 120/100/80

audit.whatIsWrong: Three interactions the brief flags as applicable never reach the page: All Out heals him, Path Maker deals true damage, and All Out's knockback launches you through a wall.
audit.why: The itemization block already says 'anti-heal early' but no matchup text tells the player why or when. Path Maker's true damage means armour or MR is the wrong purchase against his engage. And the wall knockback cuts the retreat of a champion with no dash — that is a Flash decision, not a damage decision.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds tied to All Out's healing in whys[5] and wants.you[1]; Path Maker's true damage written into whys[3]; the wall knockback and 'hold Flash for the wall, not the damage' written into late.
sources: enemyKit W flags trueDamage, R flags heal/terrain/knockup

edits.before: Level 6 Divine Ascent makes your autos ranged AoE waves and Divine Judgment grants invulnerability, so his slow melee Q can't catch you — you become the kiter.
edits.after: Ntofo Strikes is 450 range on 3.5s and needs two stacks to pull, and Path Maker is 14s — step out between them and his 525-range dash chases nothing.

edits.before: Radiant Blast shreds his Armor and MR while Starfire Spellblade chunks his missing HP, and you can R through his All Out isolation, so your spike beats his.
edits.after: Radiant Blast shreds his Armor and MR, but Path Maker's true damage ignores what you build — trade on its 14s downtime, never into the charge.

edits.before: Nashor's plus E missing-HP on-hits out-poke his passive healing from outside Q range, and his resist-swap R is useless if he can't close — your item timing wins.
edits.after: Divine Ascent makes your autos ranged AoE waves and Divine Judgment grants invulnerability, so his 450-range Q cannot reach you — you become the kiter.

edits.before: Hold R reactively and you negate his only all-in, then auto him down on his ult cooldown; he has no second answer to your range at this stage.
edits.after: Nashor's plus E missing-HP on-hits out-poke All Out's healing from outside Q range — bring Grievous Wounds and his 80s ultimate buys him nothing.

edits.before: Shred his Armor and MR with Radiant Blast (Q), then stack Starfire Spellblade (E) missing-HP on-hits to out-poke his passive healing
edits.after: Shred with Radiant Blast (Q) and buy Grievous Wounds early, then stack Starfire Spellblade (E) on-hits to out-poke All Out's healing

edits.before: You out-poke and out-kite him through your first item, but K'Sante is a genuine scaler — All Out gives him extra dashes, omnivamp, and a knockback that isolates you from your team, and a fed K'Sante can engage the moment your invulnerability ends. Use Divine Judgment reactively to deny his All Out all-in, not aggressively, and never sidelane alone into him at 2+ items where his fighter stats let him survive your nova and grind out the duel. Group instead, melt his frontline with Starfire Spellblade waves, and refuse the isolated 1v1 he scales for.
edits.after: You out-poke and out-kite him through your first item, but K'Sante is a genuine scaler — All Out gives him extra dashes, healing, and a knockback that launches you through a wall to cut your retreat. You have no dash, so hold Flash for that wall, not for the damage. Use Divine Judgment reactively to deny his All Out all-in, not aggressively, and never sidelane alone into him at 2+ items where his fighter stats let him survive your nova. Group instead, melt his frontline with Starfire Spellblade waves, and refuse the isolated 1v1 he scales for.

notes: The whys array was off by one row from Level 3 onward — the level-6 spike was printing under Level 3. Re-seated rather than patched. Left row 3 (Levels 4-5) at Skill instead of following the packet to Kayle, because early explicitly calls levels 1-5 the danger zone; claiming Kayle wins Levels 4-5 while the prose says survive them would just move the contradiction.
